title: 2026 UK ETS maritime domestic-scope port/voyage QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for maritime: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: The domestic maritime UK ETS scope generally covers maritime activities by ships of 5,000 gross tonnage or more, subject to exclusions.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the gross-tonnage threshold before scope classification.

facts.source_fact: A voyage between a UK port of call and the same or another UK port of call can be a regulated maritime activity.
In-port activity in a UK port of call is within scope and its emissions must be accounted for even without a domestic voyage.
facts.expected_handling: Do not discard in-port activity merely because there is no UK-to-UK voyage.

facts.source_fact: For UK ETS, a port includes waters landward of the outermost permanent harbour works and certain offshore installations assigned a UN/LOCODE as of 1 April 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Use the regulatory port definition and reference date.

facts.source_fact: A port of call generally involves passenger or crew embarkation/disembarkation or cargo loading/unloading.
Stops exclusively for refuelling, operational supplies, qualifying crew relief, dry dock, repairs, adverse-weather shelter or distress assistance are not port calls for this purpose.
facts.expected_handling: Apply stop-purpose exclusions before voyage boundary changes.

facts.source_fact: A regulated voyage runs from the last berth or ship-to-ship transfer in one UK port of call to the first berth or ship-to-ship transfer in the next or same UK port of call without an intervening non-UK port of call.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve berth/transfer endpoints and intervening-port logic.

facts.source_fact: Time spent moored or at anchor, including outer anchorage, can be part of a voyage under the scheme definition.
facts.expected_handling: Do not automatically classify anchorage time as out of scope.

facts.source_fact: A movement from a UK port of call to a port of call outside the UK is not regulated under the current domestic-maritime scope described by the 2026 guidance.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat consultation proposals for international scope as current domestic law.

facts.source_fact: Offshore ships are excluded up to and including 31 December 2026 and are brought into the maritime scheme from 1 January 2027 under current guidance.

guard_patterns.handling: Require >=5000 GT unless a later rule says otherwise.
Separate current domestic scope from international consultation proposals.
Scope status does not supply a measured emissions quantity.
Flag ambiguous port, stop, GT or offshore status.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; 10 x 10 = 100 controls
